question: Can the proposed participant-uncertainty correction be justified with the existing data, and does it have a substantive gap beyond conventional mixture/risk testing?
models: Only original offset seeds0,1,2; common correction parameters across seeds, scores are seed-mean losses, never ensemble scoring
truth: existing train labels reconstruct the exact original Markov prior; existing dev labels for explicitly posthoc diagnostic calibration only
comparisons_fixed_before_new_scores: original Markov and original offset endpoints
global convex mixture, alpha in[0,0.95], participant-macro BCE exact monotone-derivative bisection; verify no clipping anywhere on allowed interval
prefix-state-wise convex mixture in the same interval/objective, empty state fallback alpha0; weighted by original person recording count, not conditional equal-person reweighting
both mixtures fitted to full dev (oracle within these restricted families, never deployment performance)

both mixtures fitted separately to seven dev participants and scored only on the excluded eighth; exploratory because diagnosis already exposed dev, and overlapping calibration folds do not yield iid risk-certification samples
fixed residual logit span caps0.025 and0.1 from the previous feasibility document; no cap tuning
limits: One score audit, <=120 scalar mixture optimizations, bisection<=64steps each; no optimizer/model/backbone/seed/cap search. CPU runtime<=600seconds. Preserve any failed audit before a justified fix.
numerical_conventions: Loss tolerance1e-10. Prefer alpha0 for a flat objective; otherwise deterministic bisection root. Statewise full-dev oracle must be no worse than nested global oracle within tolerance. Lower maximum person loss does not mean every person is unharmed.
math_checks: loss clipping and convexity interior conditions
person-macro objective and no held-person truth in calibration fit
validity of basic bounded-gain betting under fixed predictor/independent calibration or sufficient conditional-mean null
exhaustive two-point null check showing overlapping cross-fit-style dependence can invalidate betting products despite marginal mean-zero losses
best-case tiny-sample counterexample showing the old Hoeffding example is not an impossibility theorem

synthetic-only conventional online expert-mixture regret control on participant-average marginal BCE, after uniform joint smoothing removes score clipping. Distinguish arbitrary-sequence cumulative regret from offline new-person risk. No sequential dev score or new real-data comparison.
promotion_gates: a valid independent calibration path or a justified dependence-aware finite-sample theorem, not iid formulas on reused/crossfit people
a substantive distinction beyond mixture/stacking, bounded logit shrinkage, LTT or betting; mere joint-pattern structure is insufficient

as an exploratory screen only: state-wise leave-person-out correction at least2percent lower mean BCE than global mixture, at least5of8 people better, and no worse maximum person loss. This does not constitute confirmation or cover arbitrary conditional correctors.
a new independent confirmation design within resources; old test stays exposed
stop: Do not promote or launch new training unless all gates have support. Failure closes this correction-certification branch; no gate/alpha bound/cap/metric changes to rescue results. Do not infer universal impossibility of all correction methods.
public_output: RESULTS.json with aggregate scores, solver accuracy, provenance and data-dependence limitations; DECISION.md with final go/no-go and direct prior comparison. Private calibration parameters and per-person vectors remain local.
